messages:
Marta Ruiz: FYI VendorX updated the PO timeline: original ETA 2025-05-10 -> now staggered: tranche A ~2025-05-04 (50%), tranche B ~2025-06-02 (remaining). They cited an assembly line firmware hold and port backlog.
Devin Park: Thats a big swing. Which SKUs affected?
Marta Ruiz: Affected: r5-42 and r5-48 lines. They say r5-32 and r4 variants unaffected.
Noah Feldman: Our marketplace can run on mixed SKU topology but not at planned throughput. If 50% arrive, our canary QPS will be ~40% of target.
Rae (sales): Sales has premium customers slated for early migration week of 5/12. We need to tell them ASAP about scope limits.
Kai (prod): Possible mitigation: shrink instance sizes for canary (lower memory model), spin extra hosted fallback capacity, or limit onboarding windows. All have tradeoffs (latency, cost, churn risk).
Marta Ruiz: Vendor offered two commercial sweeteners: 1) 45 days of waived node fees for shortfall racks, 2) a $Xk credit tied to delivery SLAs. Not formal.
Legal-BOT: Any credit or fee waiver requires an amendment with defined metrics, settlement timelines, and signatures. I can draft a short-form amendment.
Devin Park: Need a concrete engineering plan to know whether we can still ship a joint marketplace feature on 5/14. Can you quantify delta?
Noah Feldman: I'll baseline current traffic model and run 3 scenarios: full delivery (baseline), 50% early (canary-limited), and mixed-SKU fallback (reduced QPS). ETA for numbers: EOD.
Rae (sales): Meanwhile, please prep a customer note template that warns of limited slots vs full GA. Keep messaging calm.
Marta Ruiz: Action items: Ill ask VendorX for a split manifest (serial ranges + per-tranche ETA) and an official amendment proposal by 4pm PT.
Kai (prod): Action: I'll mock a routing/feature-flag plan to route overflow to hosted overlay and a cost estimate for 2 weeks of elevated spend.
Devin Park: Action: I'll calculate the preferred minimum topology that preserves SLAs for pay-tier customers.
Noah Feldman: If we cant get signed amendment clarifying credits, we should push PR date. Marketing, whats our wiggle room?
Rae (sales): Marketing asked for 72 hours of firm capacity confirmation before any co-announcement.
Marta Ruiz: VendorX replied: split manifest link incoming, preliminary 50% early, remainder ~6w later. Offering 30 days node fee waiver and "operational credit" if total delivery misses >20% of PO after 60 days.
Devin Park: Not great. That credit is fuzzy. Legal needs details.
Legal-BOT: Please request specific SLA metrics (delivery dates per tranche), remedies (credit schedule), and an explicit cap. I recommend adding a right to reschedule shipment priority if manifest changes again.
Kai (prod): Quick ask  whats our fallback SLA for customers routed to hosted overlay? We need that number to present to Sales.
Noah Feldman: Hosted overlay SLA for overflow is 99.5% with higher per-node cost. Will attach cost multiplier in my EOD model.
Rae (sales): If we delay announcement, propose a partner webinar on 5/14 to keep momentum. Sales ok with that.
Marta Ruiz: If we don't have a signed amendment and a confirmed manifest by 3pm PT tomorrow, I'm recommending we postpone the joint launch press and instead do the webinar placeholder.
Devin Park: Agreed. Please also ask VendorX for a contingency plan for partial RMA and spare parts should firmware hold persist.
VendorBot: Reminder: VendorX portal shows PO 9922 status: "partial manifest in progress".
Marta Ruiz: Manifest URL (internal): https://vendorx.share/po/9922/manifest-partial - includes tranche details and tentative serial blocks.
Noah Feldman: Got it. Running the models now. Will post a short table of projected QPS vs arrival % and overlay cost.
Legal-BOT: I'll start a short amendment draft template and share for review.
Rae (sales): Thanks team. I'll hold off proactive customer comms until we have the 3pm decision.
Marta Ruiz: Will update thread when manifest is confirmed or amendment arrives. Thanks all.
